name: Chavacano (Ternateño / Bahra)

ancestors.notes: Spanish is the lexifier; written with the Spanish alphabet.
Tagalog substrate; the earliest layer also carries a Portuguese-Malay (Ternate, Moluccas) Mardijker component.

notes: Ternateño Chabacano (locally 'Bahra'), the Spanish-lexifier creole of Ternate, Cavite, Luzon, Philippines — the oldest and most conservative Manila-Bay Chabacano, brought by Mardijker settlers from Ternate (Moluccas) in 1663. STUB WITH NO GRAPHEME TABLE: this spec maps nothing and transcribes every input to the empty string. `parent` records genealogy only and never carries data, so nothing is inherited from cbk-zam, and no `graphemes_base` edge is declared because Zamboangueño's table would be wrong here. Sippola's APiCS description of Ternate Chabacano lists neither /f/ nor /v/ in the consonant inventory, so Zamboangueño's ⟨f⟩ = [f] has no phoneme to land on, and it records a vowel-length contrast (/uː/ beside /u/) that the five-vowel Zamboangueño table does not encode. There is also no settled spelling to map: Sippola reports that Ternate Chabacano is essentially spoken, hard to find in printed media, and that Chabacano is written in different ways by different age groups. Ternateño-specific traits (a Portuguese-Malay lexical layer, distinct pronoun and TMA systems) are likewise unencoded.

sources.pages: Consonant inventory without /f/ or /v/; vowels /i e a o u/ plus long /uː/; a spoken variety with no settled spelling, written differently by different age groups.
